 Pecco Bagnaia: No hard feelings towards Aldeguer – looking ahead
 Following his crash in the MotoGP Sprint in Qatar, Pecco Bagnaia spoke out. Despite suffering broken bones, the Ducati rider remains positive. “We’ve been struggling with frustration for far too long!”

 Pecco Bagnaia had a strong weekend at the Qatar Grand Prix. On one of his favourite circuits, he finally felt comfortable again on his Ducati Desmosedici for the first time in a long while – he was among the fastest riders in both the free practice sessions and qualifying.
 Advertisement
 Advertisement
 Then came the disaster in the MotoGP Sprint on Saturday, where, whilst running in fifth place on the first lap, he was taken out by his team-mate Fermin Aldeguer. Bagnaia suffered two fractures to his right foot and several bruises all over his body in the crash. He was flown back to Italy during the night between Saturday and Sunday, where he is due to undergo surgery.

 Bagnaia has since spoken out on social media. “It feels strange to say this, but Qatar was actually one of the best weekends of the season for me. Unfortunately, things don’t always go the way you’d like them to, no matter how hard you try to turn things around – there’s nothing you can do about it,” said the two-time MotoGP World Champion. “I’m really sorry, but I want to take the positives from this weekend, because we’ve been struggling with frustration for far too long. Thank you all very much for your messages. I’m fine.” He had no harsh words for Fermin Aldeguer, who caused the crash. The Gresini rider, for his part, apologised to Bagnaia and the Ducati-Lenovo team after the race for his mistake .

 Pecco Bagnaia: First Aprilia test in jeopardy
 With his serious crash in Qatar, Pecco may well have been robbed of the chance to end his chapter with Ducati on a high note on the racetrack. It is currently uncertain whether the 29-year-old will be able to compete in Portimão in two weeks’ time and at the season finale in Valencia. His first test with the 850cc Aprilia on 1 December is also in jeopardy.
